p.i: Genevæ, Basileæ, Tiguri, & alibi, eximie dilexeris, ornaveris, et amplificaveris, infinitis documentis, luculenter sane declarasti. Et ob hanc quidem insignem tuam in me humanitatem, ac summum studium, singularemq; liberalitatem, quantum me tibi debere sentiam, et quantopere præclaram pietatem, reliquasq; virtutes tuas, quæ non in obscuro loco abditæ, sed jam in oculis Germaniæ, in luce Europæ positæ sunt, suspiciam, ἰάντιρ ἐπιτρέπει ὁ Θεὸς[?] faciam, ut omnes intelligant. Interea tenue opusculum, sed tamen ejusmodi, ut πολυμαθέστατος[?] vir, Gesnerus, elegantissimum suum ingenium in eo exercuerit, Notis meis non tam amplificatum, quàm illustrar- & a mendis non

page.notes: The Greek words in the paragraph are uncertain at several letters and are marked [?]. The line ending "illustrar-" is followed on the same line by "& a mendis non", so the sense is incomplete on this page and the word probably continues on the next page. The printed "&" before "a mendis" is a ligature-form ampersand. The "q;" after "singulare" and "reliquas" is the printed abbreviation for -que.
